To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the diagnosis of UPIAr should be established on clinical grounds (i.e., presence of inflammatory arthritis in a patient without any other known cause of arthritis) after a thorough history taking and physical examination, and that the diagnosis can be confirmed by laboratory investigations, imaging and biopsy if necessary.

in patients with undifferentiated peripheral joint inflammation, the diagnosis can be established by clinical history, physical examination, laboratory tests, radiography, MRI, ultrasound and synovial histology.

in patients with UPIA, a careful history and physical examination is mandatory, and that the following investigations are helpful in the diagnosis, prognosis and follow-up: acute phase reactants (CRP and ESR), rheumatoid factor and ACPA (anti-CCP) testing, ultrasound, MRI and genetic markers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) differential diagnosis and investigations in the early stages of UPIA; (2) clinical, laboratory and imaging assessments for the diagnosis and prognosis of UPIA in established disease; (3) predictors of persistence (and chronicity) of UPIA and (4) monitoring of clinical disease in UPIA.
the development of a set of evidence-based recommendations on the investigation and follow up of UPIA.
the development of evidence-based recommendations on the investigation and follow up of undifferentiated peripheral arthritides (UPA) in clinical practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the diagnostic value of the following parameters should be assessed: history and clinical examination, acute phase proteins, autoantibody profile, imaging (radiographs, MRI and/or ultrasound), genetic testing and synovial histopathology.

a patient presenting with UPIA should have a detailed history and physical examination including the assessment of extra-articular manifestations, a complete blood count, acute phase reactant, rheumatoid factor, HLA B27, and radiographs of the involved and adjacent joints.
UPIA should be investigated by a combination of clinical, laboratory and imaging assessments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3E initiative is an innovative approach to developing multinational recommendations.
we have produced a set of evidence-based and internationally agreed recommendations on how to approach and follow up UPIA.
we are able to provide recommendations on how to approach UPIA in daily practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a multidisciplinary and multinational approach to the development of clinical practice guidelines is feasible and can result in recommendations that are both evidence-based and supported and used by a broad panel of rheumatology experts.
the diagnosis of UPIAs is based on a thorough history and physical examination, with the help of a few key laboratory and imaging tools.

UPIA is a heterogeneous condition, and that a multidisciplinary approach, including a combination of clinical assessments and investigations, is needed to identify those with a higher probability of persistence (chronicity) or remission (self-limitation) and those with the highest probability of progression to rheumatoid arthritis.
